title: Review new words on these 3 days only: the 1-3-7 rule | Words That Stick #3
description:
You don't need to review new words every day. You need three short reviews, each just before you'd forget them.

Learn a word today. Then:
• Day 1 (tomorrow): see the word again, in its sentence.
• Day 3: cover it and recall it before you look.
• Day 7: use it in a new sentence of your own, out loud.

Each review resets the forgetting curve, and it falls more slowly every time. After Day 7, a word you've used yourself is much harder to forget.

The rule: review on Days 1, 3 and 7. Not every day, and not just once. Screenshot the schedule.

Quick test: you know her face, but not her name. You recognise the face, but you can't recall the name.

5 ways to say "strong", one picture each:
• firm: a good handshake
• sturdy: a ladder that stays steady when you climb it
• durable: hiking boots that last for years
• mighty: a huge old oak tree
• muscular: a weightlifter's arms

Try it tomorrow: see today's new words again, in their sentences.

More words for "strong": https://anotherwordfor.net/another-word-for-strong/

Next episode: why you freeze mid-sentence.

The 1-3-7 schedule is a simple practical rule. Spacing your reviews out works better than cramming them together: Cepeda, N. J., Pashler, H., Vul, E., Wixted, J. T., & Rohrer, D. (2006). Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis. Psychological Bulletin, 132(3), 354–380.
